clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within months: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and kept his distance from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch and was warned at work; your aunt Celeste left him in August; your mother lay awake over them; and your brother Callum had ear infections all winter. By May 1979, when your grandmother took a job at the library and was out every day, the shifts settle.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest, 1984–1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother being ordered to bed for the rest of her pregnancy in March 1984, within months: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep the house; your father argued with his mother over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it; and your sister Ines was born in September. These shifts settle with the birth.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis in September 1986, over the next decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments; your father phoned his father every night for news; they argued over who should help; your grandfather's chest pains began; your father drank most evenings; your grandmother could no longer stand and needed a nurse every morning; and your father and mother fought over his evenings at his parents' house. By February 1996, when your grandfather gave up his workshop and hardly left her side, the reactive shifts settle into a new steady state.

clusters.name: Callum leaving home, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home for work up north in May 1999, within months: your father and Callum argued most nights over his plans; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn; your mother took Ines with her everywhere; and by August 2000, when Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams, the shifts settle.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003–2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within months: you could not sleep more than a few hours; you stopped going in to the bookshop and were let go in May; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark; and by November, when you took a job at the garden centre and slept through the night again, the shifts settle. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then.
